content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early periods, indicating a lag in adjusting to true market dynamics.", "Sentiment spikes near the end of history correlate with forecast overshoots, suggesting sentiment amplifies model bias.", "True outcomes often show mean-reversion after initial sharp rises, contradicting the model’s upward trend.", "Model forecasts exhibit diminishing accuracy as the 30-day horizon extends, especially when sentiment is flat or negative.", "Forecast bias is more pronounced when sentiment is low, indicating sentiment dampens model confidence.", "Models fail to capture sharp downward corrections in later periods, suggesting underestimation of volatility.", "Sentiment history with non-zero values at the end of the history window correlates with higher forecast accuracy in subsequent periods.", "Forecast models should incorporate sentiment as a dynamic adjustment factor to reduce bias and improve lag correction."]}
